title: Opening and Reading

fakeFiles.story.txt:
Once upon a time.
A robot found a map.
The end.

goal: In this lesson you will learn how to open a practice file and read its whole text with read().
idea: To read a practice file: f = open("story.txt"), then text = f.read(), then f.close(). read() gives you the whole file as one string. Later you will learn a safer style with with.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change open("story.txt") to open("hello.txt"). Press Run. Output should be the hello message.

practice.text: Open hello.txt, read it, close it, and print the text.
practice.hint: After open, call f.read() and save it in text. Then close the file and print(text). Not an empty print().
practice.starterTip: Use text = f.read() on the blank line, then print(text) in the last print().
practice.gradingNote: Pass if hello.txt is opened, read, closed, and printed.

practice.text: Read story.txt and print only the first 16 characters using a slice.
practice.hint: A slice uses square brackets: text[start:end]. The first 16 characters are text[0:16]. Or just text[:16].
practice.starterTip: Print print(text[:16]) so you see "Once upon a time." without the rest of the story.
practice.starter:
f = open("story.txt")
text = f.read()
f.close()
# Print first 16 characters
print()
practice.gradingNote: Pass if a 16-character slice prints (Once upon a time).

quiz.question: What does f.read() return?

options.text: The whole file as one string

quiz.correct: read() loads the entire file into one string.
quiz.wrong: f.read() gives you the file's text as a string.

quiz.question: After you finish reading with open(), what should you do?
quiz.correct: close() finishes using the file cleanly.
quiz.wrong: Call f.close() when done (or use with later).

quiz.question: Which opens story.txt for reading?
quiz.correct: open with the file name starts reading.
